primary.notes: Round-trips to #FFB020, the brand mark's fill. The light theme uses oklch(58% 0.17 75) instead; one brand amber does not mean one token value per theme.

dev.notes: The one hue nothing else in the palette uses; it separates a development window from the release one at a glance.

border.notes: Every divider, every panel edge, and the window's own outline against the desktop. Always 1px.

muted-foreground.notes: Counts, SHAs, timestamps, section headers, and every icon affordance at rest.

secondary-foreground.notes: Where repeated text rests before hover or selection promotes it to foreground.

title.purpose: Anything you read to navigate: tab labels, sidebar project and session rows, commit subjects, menu items, buttons.

body.purpose: The same 14px unweighted: dialog prose, settings descriptions, viewer content.

label.purpose: Metadata, status and section headers. PROJECTS, a turn count, `missing`, the indexer line.

mono.purpose: Terminal output, SHAs, file paths, branch chips.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Every surface that stays on screen. Depth is four lightness steps and a hairline border.

shadows.name: floating-md
shadows.purpose: Dropdown and context menus, popovers, dialogs — surfaces that are temporary.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.value: ring-1 ring-border over the secondary ground, box-shadow: none
shadows.purpose: The one row or tab currently being dragged. A ring, not a border — a border appearing would change the element's height mid-gesture.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: The default and usually only transition: hover and focus are colour changes.

motion.name: running-pulse
motion.purpose: The working status dot, opt-in. Granted to the single dot in a session header, withheld from the sidebar and tab strip.

motion.name: refresh-spin
motion.value: spin 1s linear infinite, cleared on animationiteration
motion.purpose: A manual refresh reports while it works and stops on a rotation boundary. Deliberately not behind motion-safe: with the animation suppressed the iteration event never fires and the state latches forever.

breakpoints.name: none
breakpoints.purpose: A desktop app with a minimum window size. Side panels are user-resized, not media-queried; density is constant across widths.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one amber control on a surface: the action that commits or confirms.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 32px; padding: 6px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--primary, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(16% 0.008 250)); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, oklch(16% 0.008 250)), 0 0 0 4px var(--ring, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Everything beside the primary action. A tonal step, never a second accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 32px; padding: 6px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--secondary, oklch(22% 0.008 250)); color: var(--secondary-foreground, oklch(82% 0.006 250)); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--secondary, oklch(22% 0.008 250)) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, oklch(16% 0.008 250)), 0 0 0 4px var(--ring, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: The house style for every icon-only control. No background in any state; the icon itself takes amber on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-icon-btn" title="Refresh"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M21 12a9 9 0 1 1-2.64-6.36"/><path d="M21 3v6h-6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { display: inline-flex; flex-shrink: 0; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 2px; border: none; background: transparent; border-radius: 4px; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)) 70%, transparent); cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-icon-btn svg { width: 14px; height: 14px; pointer-events: none; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-icon-btn:hover { color: var(--primary, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); background: transparent; } .ds-icon-btn:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--ring, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-icon-btn:disabled { pointer-events: none; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)) 30%, transparent); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: 32px field sized to sit level with a default button. Focus is the same amber ring every control uses.
components.css: .ds-input { display: flex; width: 100%; height: 32px; padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(22% 0.008 250)); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--background, oklch(16% 0.008 250)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(96% 0.004 250)); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, oklch(16% 0.008 250)), 0 0 0 4px var(--ring, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Session Tab
components.description: One tab per live agent session, with a status dot on the left and a close affordance that appears on hover. Active takes a tonal ground, never an accent one.
components.html:
refactor the indexer
write the release notes
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 4px 0; } .ds-tab { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 30px; max-width: 240px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--foreground, oklch(96% 0.004 250)); } .ds-tab--active { background: var(--secondary, oklch(22% 0.008 250)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(96% 0.004 250)); font-weight: 500; } .ds-tab-label { min-width: 0; flex: 1; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-tab-close { display: inline-flex; padding: 2px; margin-right: -4px; border: none; background: transparent; border-radius: 4px; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)) 70%, transparent); opacity: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms, opacity 150ms; } .ds-tab-close svg { width: 14px; height: 14px; } .ds-tab:hover .ds-tab-close { opacity: 1; } .ds-tab-close:hover { color: var(--primary, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-dot { display: inline-block; width: 8px; height: 8px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-dot--working { background: var(--color-status-working, oklch(68% 0.17 150)); } .ds-dot--waiting { background: var(--color-status-waiting, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-dot--stopped { background: var(--color-status-stopped, oklch(55% 0.01 250)); }

components.name: Ref Chip
components.description: The app's recurring silhouette: a bordered 4px pill tinted from one hue. Branch refs, tags and the development-build marker all use the same geometry.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 1px 4px; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 4px; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "Fira Code", monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25; max-width: 55%; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip--branch { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lane-0, oklch(70% 0.15 255)) 30%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--lane-0, oklch(70% 0.15 255)) 12%, transparent); color: var(--lane-0, oklch(70% 0.15 255)); } .ds-chip--dev { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--dev, oklch(68% 0.19 300)) 30%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--dev, oklch(68% 0.19 300)) 12%, transparent); color: var(--dev, oklch(68% 0.19 300)); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; }

components.css: .ds-menu { min-width: 200px; padding: 4px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(25% 0.008 250)); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--popover, oklch(18% 0.008 250)); color: var(--popover-foreground, oklch(96% 0.004 250)); box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-menu-label { padding: 4px 8px; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-menu-item { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 28px; padding: 4px 8px 4px 28px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-menu-item:hover { background: var(--secondary, oklch(22% 0.008 250)); } .ds-menu-item--on { position: relative; } .ds-menu-item--on::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 10px; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--primary, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-menu-sep { height: 1px; margin: 4px -4px; background: var(--border, oklch(25% 0.008 250)); }

components.css: .ds-rows { display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 4px; background: var(--card, oklch(18% 0.008 250)); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 28px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 4px; color: var(--secondary-foreground, oklch(82% 0.006 250)); font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-row:hover { color: var(--foreground, oklch(96% 0.004 250)); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--secondary, oklch(22% 0.008 250)) 60%, transparent); } .ds-row--selected { background: var(--secondary, oklch(22% 0.008 250)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(96% 0.004 250)); } .ds-row-label { min-width: 0; flex: 1; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-row-meta { flex-shrink: 0; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(56% 0.006 250)); font-size: 12px; } .ds-dot { display: inline-block; width: 8px; height: 8px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-dot--waiting { background: var(--color-status-waiting, oklch(81.3% 0.165 75)); } .ds-dot--stopped { background: var(--color-status-stopped, oklch(55% 0.01 250)); }

narrative.overview:
factorai is a dark console you sit in front of all day while agents work. Its job is not to be looked at; its job is to be glanced at. Everything is arranged so that a developer returning to the window after twenty minutes away can tell, without reading, which sessions are still working, which one wants them, and which stopped. That is why the surface is quiet almost everywhere: a control room where every panel glows is a control room where nothing means anything.

The system is built from four near-black lightness steps at one hue (250) and a single warm accent. Colour is spent, not applied. Amber means your move — it is the accent, the ring, the brand mark and the waiting status, all at the same value, so the one thing that asks for the human always looks the same. Green means working, grey means inert, violet means this is the development build. Every other hue in the app is categorical rather than semantic: the commit graph's eight lane colours mean only "not the same as my neighbour".

Density is deliberate and non-negotiable. Rows are 28-30px, type has exactly two sizes, chrome heights are fixed rather than derived from their tallest child, and icon affordances paint no background at any time. The reference points are Linear's construction discipline and Factorio's palette; the anti-reference is a 16px-body web app with generous padding, which at this row count reads as a different, chunkier application borrowed from elsewhere.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first: the dark theme is the identity, not a mode; a light theme exists and is a translation, never a tint.
Two type sizes, 14px and 12px, with no third step.
One accent, used where the human must act — and almost nowhere else.
Flat: depth is four lightness steps and a hairline border.
Quiet until asked: affordances appear on hover; only state stays lit.
Machined chrome: explicit heights, hairline dividers, no decoration.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means the human's turn. It is the accent, the ring, the mark and the waiting status at a single value, and it must not be spent on decoration, on a chart series, or on a state that resolves itself. If two ambers would ever sit three percent apart on screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Focus-Not-Default Rule
rules.body: Full foreground is a focus, not a default. Text repeated down a list rests at secondary-foreground and takes foreground from its row's hover; a selected row keeps foreground permanently, because selection is a state and not a hover. A column where every row is at 96% lightness has no focus at all.

rules.name: The Chrome-Is-One-Colour Rule
rules.body: The previous rule is about rows in a list, not about chrome. Top-bar icons are all one colour, and a toggled-on control does not brighten: state that a surface already shows needs aria-pressed, not a second colour.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two type sizes and 14px is the floor for anything you read to navigate. There is no 13px step and there must not be one, so the only question a new string raises is which of the two it is. Hand-written sizes are how the scale erodes; the single standing exception is a 16px avatar's initials.

rules.name: The Shrink-The-Padding Rule
rules.body: Making a component denser means reducing its padding, never its labels. A menu row is tightened from 32px to 28px by its vertical padding, and its item text stays at 14px.

rules.name: The Fixed-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Every chrome row declares its height. If a child can grow, it truncates or scrolls; it does not push its container.

rules.name: The One-Fact Row Rule
rules.body: 28px is the height of a row carrying one fact. A row that describes an object rather than an action may stack a 12px subtitle under its label — a checkout picker row does — because a name and a branch side by side in one row truncate each other down to the prefix they share.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface that stays on screen gets tone and a hairline. A surface that appears over the app and will be dismissed gets a shadow. Nothing gets both a shadow and a tonal step to say the same thing twice.

rules.name: The Lifted-Row Rule
rules.body: An element being dragged says so with the model's own two devices — the secondary tonal step and a hairline ring — and not with a shadow. A dragged row is still part of the list it is in: it is going to land there, not be dismissed, so a shadow would claim the wrong thing. Tone alone is not enough, because the selected row it may pass over already carries it, which is what the ring is for.

rules.name: The Pointer Base Rule
rules.body: Anything clickable shows cursor: pointer, granted by one base rule covering button, a[href], select, summary, label[for] and the ARIA interactive roles — never a utility class per control, which gets forgotten exactly where a control is hand-rolled. Disabled controls are excluded: a pointer on something inert is a lie.

dos: Do use one of the two type sizes — 14px to navigate by, 12px for metadata, status and section headers.
Do give every chrome row an explicit height, and let its children truncate.
Do use IconButton for every icon-only control, and let its hover be the icon taking amber.
Do keep repeated text at secondary-foreground and let hover or selection promote it to foreground.
Do import the chip shape from its constant rather than re-deriving its border, radius, padding and size.
Do let a chevron take colour from whatever the click target is — its own hover when it is the target, its row's when the row is.
Do ship a keyboard path beside every pointer gesture — a feature only a mouse can reach is half a feature.
Do give a light-theme token its own value rather than a tint of the dark one; lane colours drop ~20 lightness points and move per hue between themes.
Do report while a manual refresh works, and stop on a rotation boundary so a 20ms refetch is one clean turn rather than a one-frame flash.
donts: Don't spend amber on anything that is not the human's turn to act.
Don't paint a background behind an icon button in any state, including hover, active and toggled-on.
Don't brighten a chrome icon to show it is toggled on — the surface it toggles is already visible; use aria-pressed.
Don't introduce a third type size, and don't hand-write one to sneak past the scale.
Don't add a shadow to a surface that stays on screen; tone and a hairline are the elevation model.
Don't animate more than one thing at a time in a list. Status animation is opt-in and belongs to the single dot that describes the current view.
Don't use HTML5 drag-and-drop; it is dead in this shell on macOS. Drag with pointer events.
Don't put a raw input, button or select in app code — the primitives carry the scale, and an element that opts out of them is the next inline override.
Don't grant the pointer cursor with a per-control class; extend the base rule instead, so disabled controls keep being excluded.
